summary:
## 🌟 Summary
**Ultralytics 8.4.177 makes SAM prompts work consistently across image directories and video frames, alongside fixes that improve export reliability, training resumes, and prediction inputs.**

## 📊 Key Changes
- **SAM prompts now persist across a source:** Prompts supplied for a directory or video are applied to every image or frame, rather than just the first. Prompt coordinates are also scaled without changing caller-owned NumPy arrays or tensors.
- **More reliable model exports and inference:** Dynamic OpenVINO exports are pinned to the requested image size on Intel NPUs, which require fixed input dimensions. ONNX GPU inference now falls back to a compatible execution path when output shapes contain symbolic dimensions.
- **Safer training and checkpoint recovery:** Short training runs now take an optimizer step instead of potentially ending without updating the model. RMSprop checkpoints preserve small gradient-history values, helping resumed training avoid unexpectedly large updates.
- **More consistent prediction inputs:** PIL images now respect EXIF orientation, and source lists download only actual HTTP(S) URLs—so local paths beginning with `http` are not mistaken for links.
- **Improved experiment tracking and integrations:** Integration settings are read for each training run. W&B fixes improve final plot logging, offline resume IDs, project/run naming, and cleanup after interrupted or failed runs.
- **Documentation and workflow updates:** Guides clarify validation image geometry, W&B usage, Platform export options, and contribution testing advice. CI failure alerts are centralized, and runner images regain dependencies needed for Codecov signature checks.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- **SAM users** can provide prompts once and get the intended segmentation behavior throughout a folder or video, whether using Python, streaming, or the CLI.
- **Training and deployment users** should see fewer failures on Intel NPUs and dynamic-output ONNX models, while checkpoint resumes and very short runs behave more reliably.
- **Everyday prediction workflows** handle phone-camera images and mixed source lists more predictably.
- **No new model architecture is introduced** in this release; the emphasis is on more dependable prediction, training, export, integrations, and documentation.

## What's Changed
* Name Platform export options and update the contributing guide's test advice by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26659
* Fix dynamic OpenVINO exports failing to compile on the Intel NPU by @onuralpszr in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26656
* Centralize workflow failure alerts in the GitHub App by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26661
* Restore Codecov signature dependencies in runner images by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26662
* Add https://youtu.be/TBEPfu2IMXE to docs by @RizwanMunawar in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26649
* Download only http(s) URLs in prediction source lists by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26660
* Preserve RMSprop second moments when saving checkpoints by @Vaishnavi220506 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26652
* Apply EXIF orientation to PIL prediction inputs by @Nikhi00718 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26650
* Take at least one optimizer step in runs shorter than the accumulation interval by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26663
* Fix ONNX GPU binding for symbolic output shapes by @aswanth-07 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26657
* Fix W&B final plots, resume id, project and run names, and failed-run cleanup by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26654
* Document rectangular validation geometry in val mode docs by @lu123bing in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26653
* Read integration settings per trainer and keep the events session id off the seeded RNG by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26658
* 8.4.177 Fix SAM prompts across images and video frames by @8rulerstar in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26651

## New Contributors
* @lu123bing made their first contribution in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26653

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/compare/v8.4.176...v8.4.177

summary:
Update MicroDuck, G1, and ANYmal-D with transparent joysticks inside the viewport and compact pause/reset controls. MicroDuck starts standing; dragging the robot applies a fixed 2 N horizontal push, while dragging the background orbits the camera. Mouse/touch release, cancellation, and focus loss stop the interaction.

This UI-only update reuses the original physics, policy, and geometry files. The archive includes unchanged `v1/` and `v2/` payloads plus `v3/`; deploy all three directories. It adds about 28 KB to the previous compressed archive. No simulation rebuild is required.

Source: [reference PR #7974](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/pull/7974), [viewer revision `62607a3e4`](https://github.com/maxkra15/IsaacLab/commit/62607a3e49b75ae73e55cd90eeaf661dd4fb000a). Site source snapshot: NVIDIA GitLab `omniverse/isaac/isaaclab-browser-demos`, commit `15986c4`. Documentation integration: [#8543](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/pull/8543).

Validation: all twelve demos stepped with finite state and no JavaScript errors. MicroDuck standing, walking, turning, fixed-force mouse/touch pushes, camera orbit, two simultaneous touch joysticks, cancellation, pause/reset, and mobile layout passed. Simulation timing remained near real time in the measured run. Third-party license notices are retained.

SHA-256 (`isaaclab-browser-demos-v3.tar.gz`): `a860b7e59793d553545b76abf2b09d15ff20685972ec803c6c07163e6678f64a`.

summary:

Build pins and policy/asset provenance are included in `v2/README.md` and the manifest. Third-party license notices are included.

Validation: all twelve demos loaded and stepped with finite state and no JavaScript errors; MicroDuck walking/turning, keyboard release, mouse push/release, pause/reset, mobile layout, and elapsed simulation time passed. These previews are not policy evaluation benchmarks.
